message: 36M. I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area. No fever, no trouble breathing.

basis.quote: I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area.
basis.interpretation: Active contact dermatitis with pruritic vesicular rash on bilateral forearms, progressing locally since Saturday exposure.
Patient denies constitutional symptoms and respiratory involvement, reducing concern for systemic or severe allergic reaction.

output.reason: Localized contact dermatitis requires clinician assessment for topical treatment and guidance on progression monitoring, but no emergency features or same-day physical dependency is evident.

Reported itchy blistery rash limited to both forearms after poison ivy exposure, spreading only within that area, with fever and breathing trouble denied; no decision-critical uncertainty, functional impairment, treatment failure or medication request reported that requires a clinician task now. Over-the-counter measures with clear escalation triggers are appropriate.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now with over-the-counter itch remedies from your pharmacist; a poison ivy rash typically stays where the plant sap touched skin and settles over days. Wash clothing and tools, since the sap can linger. If the rash spreads well beyond your forearms, involves your face, eyes or genitals, becomes severe, or you develop fever, mouth or eye sores, or skin that looks infected, see a clinician promptly — book an urgent in-person visit that day. If you develop trouble breathing or throat tightness, call 911.
